items.title: The Lusztig–Kashiwara form, parameter and coproduct dictionary
items.statement:
Set Lusztig's parameter v=q^-1, so v_i=q_i^-1. The presentation map E_i^L↦E_i,F_i^L↦F_i,K_h^L↦K_(-h) is an algebra isomorphism after parameter transport, preserves the divided-power A-forms and intertwines bar. It carries the Lusztig coproduct to the OPPOSITE of the fixed library coproduct ΔE_i=E_i⊗K_i^-1+1⊗E_i, ΔF_i=F_i⊗1+K_i⊗F_i. Therefore swapping tensor factors carries the Lusztig quasi-R convention to a bar-coproduct intertwiner in U^+⊗U^- for this Δ.
On the abstract half f, θ_i maps to F_i and θ_i^(n) to F_i^(n), and the twisted coproduct multiplication becomes (x1⊗x2)(y1⊗y2)=q^(−(deg x2,deg y1))x1y1⊗x2y2. Lusztig's form B_L on degree nu=Σ_i nu_i alpha_i is B_L=C_nu B_K, C_nu=∏_i(1−q_i²)^−nu_i, where B_K is the normalized Kashiwara half form. This is a color-degree scaling, a unit≡1 atq=0, not a single scalar or equality of forms on all degrees. In rank one B_L(F_i^(n),F_i^(n))=∏_(r=1)^n(1−q_i^(2r))^-1. The corresponding normalized Drinfeld pairing D on U^+_nu×U^-_(−nu) is D(x,y)=d_nu^-1 B_K(ιx,y), d_nu=∏_i(q_i−q_i^-1)^nu_i and ι(E_i)=F_i. Thus D(E_i,F_j)=delta_ij/(q_i−q_i^-1). Its coevaluation is exactly the transported/flipped Lusztig quasi-R component; the n1 coefficient is q_i−q_i^-1.
items.strategy:
Check the complete presentation. Under v=q^-1 and K_h^L↦K_(-h), toral conjugation becomes K_(-h)E_iK_h=q^(-<h,alpha_i>)E_i=v^(<h,alpha_i>)E_i, with the analogous F relation. Both numerator and denominator of the mixed commutator change sign, so [E_i,F_i]=(K_i−K_i^-1)/(q_i−q_i^-1) is preserved. Symmetric [n]_(v_i)=[n]_(q_i), so the Serre coefficients and divided powers are unchanged. The map is involutive with inverse parameter transport and toral inversion. Bar commutes with it on every generator and the coefficient field. The actual printed sourceΔ_L E_i=E_i⊗1+K_i^L⊗E_i maps to E_i⊗1+K_i^-1⊗E_i=Δ^op E_i; sourceΔ_L F_i=F_i⊗(K_i^L)^-1+1⊗F_i maps to F_i⊗K_i+1⊗F_i=Δ^op F_i. Thus tensor flip, not an unexplained doubled-torus scalar, supplies the correct orientation.
The source half twisted product has v^(deg x2,deg y1), becoming q^negative, exactly the normalized Kashiwara shuffle convention. Extracting the θ_i⊗(remaining word) coefficient of the twisted coproduct gives the recursion e_i′(F_jQ)=delta_ij Q+q_i^(−a_ij)F_j e_i′Q. Lusztig's source generator norm is(1−v_i^-2)^-1=(1−q_i²)^-1, so B_L(F_iP,Q)=(1−q_i²)^-1 B_L(P,e_i′Q). Induct on word height, using the Kashiwara adjunction and C_nu=(1−q_i²)^-1C_(nu−alpha_i), to prove B_L=C_nu B_K in every degree. Both are homogeneous, normalized at1 and descend through the same Serre ideal, so this word induction proves the full quotient dictionary. The rank-one norm follows from B_K(F_i^(n),F_i^(n))=1/[n]_(q_i²)! and C_(n alpha_i)=(1−q_i²)^-n, canceling the ordinary Gaussian factorial factors.
Lusztig4.1.2(b) has coefficient(−1)^ht(nu)∏v_i^nu_i times the coevaluation of B_L. Its dual tensor is C_nu^-1 times that of B_K. After parameter transport and tensor flip, symmetry of the homogeneous Gram matrix lets either positive or negative basis be listed first; the overall scalar is(−1)^ht∏q_i^-nu_i C_nu^-1=∏(q_i−q_i^-1)^nu_i=d_nu. Hence it is the coevaluation of D, proving the stated general formula and n1 normalization. This uses complete source form/coproduct identities and a full word-height induction, not merely the rank-one value.

items.title: The bar lattice and the divided-power integral lattice of a based module
items.statement:
Fix $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ and the crystal limiting ring $A_0\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ of [[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]], and put $A_\infty:=\psi(A_0)$, the image of $A_0$ under the semilinear involution $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, i.e. the ring of rational functions regular at $q=\infty$; $A_0$ and $A_\infty$ are the rational local rings at0 and infinity; the integral affine chart coordinate rings are Z[q] and Z[q^-1].

Let $M$ be one of $U_q^-$ or $V(\lambda)=L(\lambda)$ ($\lambda\in P^+$). Equip $M$ with the bar involution $\psi$ of [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]]: on $U_q^-$ the semilinear algebra involution $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(F_i)=F_i$, $\psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$; on $V(\lambda)$ the induced semilinear involution determined by $Pv_\lambda\mapsto\psi(P)v_\lambda$ (well defined because the highest vector is fixed). Let $M_A\subseteq M$ be the divided-power integral form: $M_A=U_A^-$ for $M=U_q^-$, and $M_A=V_A(\lambda):=U_A^-v_\lambda$ for $M=V(\lambda)$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]; $U_A^-$ and $V_A(\lambda)$ are $\psi$-stable). Let $L$ be the Kashiwara crystal lattice of $M$ over $A_0$: $L=L(\infty)$ for $U_q^-$ and $L=L(\lambda)$ for $V(\lambda)$ ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]]).

Define the **bar lattice** $L^-:=\psi(L)$, an $A_\infty$-submodule of $M$, and the **balanced part** $E:=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$. The definition keeps three structures on the same $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space strictly separate: the $A$-module $M_A$, which is not assumed free and not claimed to be contained in $L$; the free $A_0$-module $L$; and the free $A_\infty$-module $L^-$. No equality $L^-=L$, no inclusion $M_A\subseteq L$, no freeness of $M_A$ and no identification $E=M_A$ are asserted; freeness is a conclusion of the balanced-triple construction, whereas E is a Z-module of global lifts and is not equal to the Laurent lattice M_A. The bar lattice is not the form-dual (upper) lattice, which is defined later on this page. Intersections M_A∩L and M_A∩L^- are respectively Z[q]- and Z[q^-1]-modules, generally not A-modules. The balanced part E is a Z-module; its Laurent extension A⊗_Z E is the full integral module once globalization is proved. More generally a based integrable module (M,B) here means exactly: B is a homogeneous field basis; M_A=⊕_b A b is U_A-stable; the semilinear involution fixing B is U/bar compatible; and L0=⊕_b A0 b with residue B is a crystal local basis at0. These are Lusztig27.1.2(a)–(d) after v=q^-1 and the integrable Bao–Wang extension. Such data do not automatically imply integral Θ action on an arbitrary based pair. A based subobject is a U-submodule spanned by a subset of B; a based quotient is its quotient with the complementary basis images. Based morphisms send B to the target basis or0 and have kernels spanned by the killed basis subset. These exact integral/bar-compatible maps, not arbitrary field summands, are used in tensor inheritance.
items.strategy: A definition fixing the three lattices. The involution $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ maps $A_0$ isomorphically onto $A_\infty$, so $\psi(L)$ is an $A_\infty$-lattice generating $M$. $\psi(M_A)=M_A$ holds on $U_A$ by [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]], and $V_A(\lambda)$ is $\psi$-stable because $\psi(F_{i_1}^{(r_1)}\cdots F_{i_k}^{(r_k)}v_\lambda)=F_{i_1}^{(r_1)}\cdots F_{i_k}^{(r_k)}v_\lambda$ on divided-power monomials. Nothing is asserted about $M_A\cap L$; in particular the definition hides no integral-freeness assumption and no self-duality of the lower lattice. No choice principle is used. The general four based conditions are checked independently; the associated bar fixes a field basis but U compatibility and U_A stability are real requirements. Basis-subset subobjects give saturated free integral sublattices and free complementary quotients. Their bars are the restrictions/quotients of the ambient bar, and their crystal local data are inherited because their subset/kernel is closed under the module action and the residue operators. This is the actual source27.1.3–27.1.4 interface, not an assumed integral splitting of a semisimple field module.

items.title: Balanced triples over the two charts of $\mathbb P^1$ and the globalization map
items.statement:
Let V be finite dimensional over Q(q), M⊂V an A=Z[q,q^-1]-submodule spanning V, and L0,L∞ free full rational chart lattices over A0,A∞. Put L_Z=M∩L0, L_Z^-=M∩L∞, E_Z=M∩L0∩L∞. The integral triple is balanced if the canonical Z-linear map E_Z→L_Z/qL_Z=(M∩L0)/(M∩qL0) is an isomorphism. Its inverse is the integral globalization map on the integral residue subgroup. Rational balancedness is the corresponding isomorphism Q⊗_Z E_Z→L0/qL0, after extending the integral subgroup by Q. In applications the integral subgroup is ZB, and its globalization gives the lower lifts G(b).
The two-chart lemma proves M≅A⊗_Z E_Z, L_Z≅Z[q]⊗_Z E_Z and L_Z^-≅Z[q^-1]⊗_Z E_Z. If E_Z has a finite Z-basis B_E whose rational residue classes are a basis of L0/qL0, these lifts give bases of M,L0,L∞ over A,A0,A∞. Thus actual A-freeness follows from integral balancedness PLUS the proved free integral residue basis; it is not automatic for an arbitrary non-finitely-generated Z-submodule. All definitions apply componentwise to the finite root/label spaces.
items.strategy: The kernel in the residue map is M∩qL0=qL_Z because M is closed under q±. Integral balancedness is therefore an assertion about a Z-subgroup in the rational residue field. The two-chart lemma supplies its extension isomorphisms without assuming M free. A finite Z-basis of E_Z extends to a free A-basis of M; rational full chart spans give the A0/A∞ bases. For the quantum applications, the separate integral-residue lemma and globalization induction prove exactly this missing finite Z-basis hypothesis. The distinction prevents a Q-residue isomorphism from falsely identifying a Z-balanced intersection with a rational vector space.

items.title: The integral residue lattices $L_A(\infty)$ and $L_A(\lambda)$
items.statement:
Let A=Z[q,q^-1], with rational DVRs A0 atq=0 and A∞ atq=∞. Put M_A=U_A^- or V_A(lambda)=U_A^-v_lambda, L=L∞ or Llambda, and L^-=bar L. The integral residue lattice is L_Z=M_A∩L, a Z[q]-module, and its bar lattice is L_Z^-=M_A∩L^-, a Z[q^-1]-module. Its balanced intersection E_Z=M_A∩L∩L^- is a Z-module. Since q^-1M_A=M_A, M_A∩qL=qL_Z; consequently the residue map L_Z/qL_Z→L/qL is injective and is Z-linear. Its image is an integral subgroup of the rational crystal space, not the entire Q-space. No Laurent-A-linearity is asserted on the residue lattice or map.
The field projection pi_lambda restricts to an A-linear surjection U_A^-→V_A(lambda) and sends L_Z(infinity) into L_Z(lambda), by the already proved grand-loop lattice projection. The module V_A is U_A-stable: reordering reduces actions on v_lambda to negative divided powers and toral Gaussian scalars in A, with all positive generators killing the top except the unit. No global freeness, residue spanning or balancedness is assumed here. The integral residue subgroup for the negative half is proved below to be ZB∞; the module subgroup ZBλ is a consequence of globalization.
items.strategy: Intersections inherit Z[q] or Z[q^-1] actions because these rings preserve the corresponding rational DVR lattices and the Laurent integral module. They do not inherit q^-1 or q actions on the wrong chart. If x∈M_A∩qL, then q^-1x∈M_A∩L, proving the exact quotient kernel. Pi preserves both the integral form by definition and the rational crystal lattice by the completed grand loop, so it preserves the intersection. Reordering and the integral highest character prove V_A stability, using actual A Gaussian scalars rather than the false equality U_A^0v=Q(q)v. These are definitions and already-proved supplier consequences, independent of global integral bases.

items.title: The root-height completion for weightwise quasi-$R$ intertwiners
items.statement:
For the fixed library coproduct use the diagonal root-height completion C_hat=∏_(nu∈Q+)U^+[nu]⊗U^-[-nu], with multiplication (AB)_nu=Σ_(beta+gamma=nu)A_beta B_gamma. Each component sum is finite because I is finite and root coefficients are nonnegative integers. For intertwining with ΔU, use the ambient completed tensor square obtained from Lusztig4.1.1 by the actual v=q^-1, K_h↦K_-h presentation map and tensor flip; equivalently all generator identities are read coefficientwise in the root grading. The tensor orientation is POSITIVE first, NEGATIVE second.
A family acts on m_mu⊗n_eta by its finite sum whenever U^+_nu m_mu⊗U^-_-nu n_eta vanishes for all sufficiently high nu. This holds if the first factor has finite-union bounded-above support, or if the second factor is a lowest module with bounded-below support. For both factors in finite-weight-space O_int the relevant fixed total-weight subspace is finite dimensional, and every tail beyond a finite degree acts0 there. An infinite series is not evaluated on a two-sided-unbounded pair without this explicit finiteness condition. This completion and Θ_0=1 are field-level data; no universal-R, braiding or integral coefficient property is asserted here.
items.strategy: A fixed nu has only finitely many nonnegative coefficient decompositions, proving convolution is defined and associative. The exact presentation/flip map carries the complete source topology to the fixed coproduct convention; no Drinfeld-double identification is assumed. For a homogeneous first input mu under upper cones lambda_j−Q+, any potentially nonzero positive raising degree satisfies nu≤lambda_j−mu componentwise for some j, a finite set. A lowest second input similarly requires nu≤eta−its lower label. Finite sums of homogeneous inputs give vectorwise finiteness. If both factor supports are finite unions of upper cones, a fixed total label gamma has only finitely many decompositions (lambda_j−beta)+(lambda_k′−beta′)=gamma, because beta+beta′ is fixed in Q+; finite weight components then give finite total-weight dimension and a uniform tail bound. No vanishing is inferred merely from finite-dimensional weight spaces without support bounds.

items.title: The Drinfeld pairing between the positive and negative quantum halves
items.statement: Let B_K be the normalized Kashiwara half form and let ι:U^+→U^- send E_i↦F_i (equivalently use the library's signed Chevalley involution with the compensating degree sign). For x of positive degree nu and y of negative degree−nu define D(x,y)=d_nu^-1 B_K(ιx,y), d_nu=∏_i(q_i−q_i^-1)^nu_i, and set different-degree pairings0. Then D(E_i,F_j)=delta_ij/(q_i−q_i^-1), and D(E_i^(n),F_i^(n))=q_i^(−n(n−1)/2)/([n]_i!(q_i−q_i^-1)^n). The pairing with generator value1 is B_K transport, not this quasi-R/Drinfeld normalization. The completed normalized tensor uses the D-dual basis. On the simple-root Borel extensions its toral normalization is D(K_nu,K_mu)=q^((nu,mu)), with mixed toral/root generator pairings0 and counit normalization; the Hopf adjunction identities use Δ on the negative Borel and Δ^op on the positive Borel. No unchosen pairing on arbitrary extra toral directions of Pvee is asserted.
items.strategy: The positive/negative Serre presentations identify their generators; B_K is already homogeneous and defined on the actual quotient. The nonzero degree scalar d_nu gives the stated formula, with the exact generator sign fixed by ι(E_i)=F_i. The full degree/color normalization supplier proves this is the pairing whose coevaluation is the actual source-normalized quasi-R tensor after parameter transport and flip. Simple-root toral extension is specified independently by its root bilinear form and counits; its generator relations give the stated Borel convention, avoiding meaningless coproduct pairing with toral factors absent from the domain.

items.title: The balanced-triple linear algebra over $\mathbb P^1$
items.statement:
For finite-dimensional V over Q(q), let M⊂V be an A=Z[q,q^-1]-submodule spanning V and L0,L∞ full free A0,A∞ lattices. Write E=M∩L0∩L∞. (1) If E→(M∩L0)/(M∩qL0) is a Z-isomorphism, then M∩L0≅Z[q]⊗_Z E, M∩L∞≅Z[q^-1]⊗_Z E and M≅A⊗_Z E; the infinity residue map is also an isomorphism. Rational chart extension gives A0⊗_Z E≅L0 and A∞⊗_Z E≅L∞. If E has a finite Z-basis, these are actual free bases. No containment M⊂L0∩L∞ or freeness of M/E is assumed.
(2) If a Z-module F maps into M∩L0∩L∞, generates M over A, and maps injectively into both rational residues L0/qL0 and L∞/q^-1L∞, then F≅E≅(M∩L0)/(M∩qL0).
(3) More generally let N⊂M be an A-submodule with integral balanced intersection E_N=N∩L0∩L∞. If a Z-module F maps to M∩(L0+N)∩(L∞+N), generates M modulo N over A, and maps injectively into (L0+Q N)/(qL0+Q N) and (L∞+Q N)/(q^-1L∞+Q N), then M is balanced. The sequence 0→(N∩L0)/(N∩qL0)→(M∩L0)/(M∩qL0)→(L0+Q N)/(qL0+Q N) is exact, and the last image is the image of F. If F and E_N are finite free Z-modules, so is E_M, and M is free over A. These are Kashiwara91 Lemmas7.1.1–7.1.2, in integral notation; their rational base extension gives the usual Q[q±] criterion.
items.strategy:
(1) E injects into the rational residue by the hypothesis, hence is Z-torsionfree. Residue surjectivity gives M∩L0⊂Σ_(k=0)^n q^k E+M∩q^(n+1)L0 for every n, by repeatedly subtracting a lift and dividing by q (which preserves M). For x also in q^nL∞, the subtracted terms k≤n lie there; the remainder is in q^n(M∩qL0∩L∞)=0 by residue injectivity on E. Thus M∩L0∩q^nL∞=⊕_(k=0)^n q^kE. Every element of M∩L0 has a finite infinity-pole bound, so the union over n gives Z[q]E. Distinct powers are independent: in a finite relation normalize the lowest exponent and reduce modulo q, then successively remove it. Also M=Z[q±](M∩L0) by finite zero-pole bounds. The analogous infinity-pole argument gives Z[q^-1]E and the mirror residue isomorphism. Since M spans V, Q(q)E spans V; rational residue injection shows a Q-basis of QE is independent and full. Expanding in that basis, zero/infinity valuation gives the full chart extension identities. Freeness over A is claimed only if E is actually finite free over Z.
(2) Laurent expansions in phi(F) have unique finite coefficients: reduce the lowest exponent at0 using the first injection. If an expansion lies in L0 it has no negative exponent; if it lies in L∞ it has no positive exponent, by the second injection. Therefore the intersection is exactly phi(F), with the claimed residue map and factorization. This is finite Laurent linear algebra, not passage to an unjustified formal limit.
(3) Work first on each finitely generated submodule F′ of F; its rational residue injection implies Z-torsionfreeness and hence finite Z-freeness. The balanced factorization of N gives N=(N∩L0)+(N∩L∞). If x∈M∩(L0+N)∩(L∞+N), subtract an element of N to put it in L0. Its remaining discrepancy from L∞ lies in N; split that discrepancy into its zero and infinity chart parts, then subtract its zero chart part to obtain an element of M∩L0∩L∞. Thus the lifts of a finite Z-basis of F′ can be changed by N so that they lie in the simultaneous intersection. Their direct sum with E_N injects into each rational residue: in the quotient modulo QN the F′ component is forced0 by the assumed injection, and then E_N injectivity forces the remaining component0. They generate AF′+N over A. Apply (2) to obtain balancedness and the exact residue sequence there. Taking the union over finite F′ proves the general assertion, without claiming an infinite torsionfree Z-module is free. When F and E_N are finite free, the direct sum description gives E_M finite free. This reproduces the printed diagrams and avoids the native unsupported chart containment, wrong q^nL0/q^nL∞ recursion and coherent-sheaf freeness shortcut.

items.title: Integral residues of the negative half: freeness, the crystal basis and the form characterization
items.statement: For L_Z(infinity)=U_A^-∩L(infinity), its canonical injection L_Z/qL_Z→L/qL has image exactly ⊕_(b∈B∞)Z b. It is a free Z-module with basis B∞ and becomes the full rational crystal space after tensoring with Q. The normalized Kashiwara half form takes values on U_A^- in K_Z=Z[q,q^-1,(1−q^(2n))^-1:n≥1], and on L_Z in A_Z=Z[q,(1−q^(2n))^-1:n≥1]. Thus its residue pairing is Z-valued. Its coefficients in B∞ are the integer pairings with b, and its norm1 elements are B∞∪(−B∞). The operators ẽ_i,f̃_i preserve L_Z and its integral residue subgroup. No A-module structure on L_Z, no equality with the rational residue as a Z-module, and no unsigned norm1 characterization is asserted. The module integral residue basis is established in globalization.
items.strategy: The integral skew-string supplier proves every string coefficient and both half Kashiwara operators preserve U_A^-. The completed crystal theorem proves their L∞ stability. Consequently every lowering word applied to1 lies in L_Z, providing an integral representative of every b∈B∞. For P,Q in U_A^-, the exact divided-word denominator bound from the half form places B(P,Q) in K_Z: quantum factorial denominators are Laurent powers times products (1−q^(2d_i r)) divided by powers (1−q^(2d_i)), so K_Z contains every such value. This is the same normalized Kashiwara form as the q0 polarization; there is no second normalization factor between them. The post-grand-loop polarization lemma puts B(P,Q)∈A0 when P,Q∈L_Z. To prove A0∩K_Z=A_Z, take a common denominator D=∏(1−q^(2n))^e with D(0)=1 and integer Laurent numerator. Regularity at0 says exactly that numerator has no negative powers. Evaluation of A_Z at0 gives integers. Thus, for any x∈L_Z with rational residue Σ a_b b, pairing with the integral word representative of b gives a_b∈Z by orthonormality. Conversely all finite integer combinations of the representatives lie in L_Z. The kernel is qL_Z by the preceding Definition, proving the actual free integral residue quotient. For norm1, Σ a_b²=1 with integers a_b has a single coefficient+1 OR−1, so the signed assertion follows. No global integral basis has been presumed.

items.title: Reversal preserves the negative-half integral and crystal lattices
items.statement: The Q(q)-linear anti-involution star fixing each F_i reverses negative words, preserves U_A^-, commutes with bar, preserves the normalized half form, and preserves L∞ and L_Z∞ as well as their bar lattices. On the integral crystal residue it permutes B∞∪(−B∞). Only this signed lattice preservation, not an unproved unsigned star-crystal theorem, is required for gluing the string-ideal global lifts.
items.strategy: Reversing each quantum Serre relation gives the same relation after reindexing its finite sum, so star is a well-defined anti-involution; it fixes each divided generator, proving U_A^- stability, and commutes with bar because it fixes q and both maps fix the generators. The normalized word Gram formula is a sum over color-matching permutations with crossing exponents; reversing both words bijects permutations and their crossings without changing each weight, proving B(Pstar,Qstar)=B(P,Q), then extends by bilinearity and the Serre quotient. The already-proved norm characterization L∞={P:B(P,P)∈A0} gives L∞ stability, using star's isometry. Intersect with U_A^- for L_Z and apply commuting bar for the infinity chart. The signed norm1 characterization of the integral residue then shows its signed crystal set is stable. These are Kashiwara91 Proposition5.2.1/5.2.4 and Corollary6.1.2, whose printed signed conclusion is used exactly.

items.title: Integrality of the string decomposition and the divided-power string ideals
items.statement:
For the negative-half decomposition u=Σ_l F_i^(l)u_l, ker e_i'∋u_l, all u_l are in U_A^- if u∈U_A^-. The integral projector is P_i=Σ_l(−1)^l q_i^(−l(l−1)/2) F_i^(l)(e_i')^l and u_l=q_i^(l(l−1)/2)P_i(e_i')^l u. All derivation powers here are ORDINARY, not divided by [l]_i!.
Define I_(i,n)^A=U_A^-∩F_i^n U_q^-=⊕_(l≥n)F_i^(l)(ker e_i'∩U_A^-)=Σ_(l≥n)F_i^(l)U_A^- and J_(i,n)^A=pi_lambda(I_(i,n)^A)=Σ_(l≥n)F_i^(l)V_A(lambda). The latter is an A-submodule inside the field string-image subspace F_i^n V(lambda), not a U_q-submodule or U_A-stable lattice in general. Its equality with V_A∩F_i^n V is proved after the adapted global basis construction, not presumed before it.
The integral residue of I_(i,n)^A∩L∞ is the free Z-span of B∞∩f̃_i^n B∞, and the corresponding rational residue of F_i^nU^-∩L∞ is its Q-span. Integral balancedness of the zero/infinity triple is proved by the subsequent string-ideal induction. On every U_A-stable integrable module lattice M_A, if a label mu has <h_i,mu>=−n≤−1, then each u∈(M_A)_mu satisfies the finite identity u=Σ_(k≥n)(−1)^(k−n)[k−1 choose k−n]_i F_i^(k)E_i^(k)u. Thus (M_A)_mu=Σ_(k≥n)F_i^(k)(M_A)_(mu+k alpha_i). This is the exact boundary-generation supplier used in the string-ideal induction.
items.strategy:
The first part is exactly the proved ordinary-power integral skew-string supplier; no divided-derivation integrality is used (in rank one, (e_i')²/[2]_i applied to F_i^(2) gives1/(1+q_i²), not an A scalar). Unique field string positions show membership in F_i^nU^- is equivalent to all u_l=0 for l<n. Integral coefficient extraction therefore proves the direct sum with ker e_i'; the larger spaces F_i^(l)U_A^- overlap and are only a sum. Applying pi gives the stated module IMAGE sum, without asserting saturation/intersection or generator stability. For the integral residue, every b in the indicated subset has an integral representative f̃_i^n applied to an integral word representative. String component extraction preserves L∞, so the rational field image has exactly the Q-basis of those positions. The Z-valued residue pairing from the integral residue supplier forces coefficients of any integral member to be integers. This proves the Z subgroup and kernel as above, not a premature global lift.
For the boundary identity fix z=q_i, mu(h_i)=−n and an admissible string u=F_i^(m)v, Ev=0. Its top weight is2m−n, so m≥n. Rank-one divided-power formulas give F^(k)E^(k)u=[m−n+k choose k]_z[m choose k]_z u, and vanish for k>m. It suffices to prove Σ_(k=n)^m(−1)^(k−n)[k−1 choose k−n]_z[m−n+k choose k]_z[m choose k]_z=1. Here is a complete finite proof. Put Q=z², (Q;Q)_s=∏_(j=1)^s(1−Q^j), and H(t)=∏_(j=1)^(n−1)(1−Q^(-j)t)∏_(j=1)^(m−n)(1−Q^j t), of degree m−1. For every polynomial of degree≤m−1, the finite q-binomial theorem (proved by the Gaussian Pascal recurrence) yields Σ_(k=0)^m(−1)^k Q^(k(k−1)/2−k(m−1)) Gaussian_Q(m,k) H(Q^k)=0: check each monomial t^s, where the sum is ∏_(j=0)^(m−1)(1−Q^(j+s−m+1)), with a zero factor j=m−1−s. For 1≤k<n, H(Q^k)=0. For k≥n, H(Q^k)/[(Q;Q)_(n−1)(Q;Q)_(m−n)]=Gaussian_Q(k−1,n−1)Gaussian_Q(m−n+k,k). For k=0 this ratio is(−1)^(n−1)Q^(−n(n−1)/2). Multiply the zero-sum identity by(−1)^n Q^(n(n−1)/2) divided by those two factorials. Its k=0 term is−1; the remaining terms are exactly the required symmetric-binomial sum, using [a choose b]_z=z^(−b(a−b))Gaussian_Q(a,b). Their exponent is k(k−1)/2−k(m−1)+n(n−1)/2. Hence the remaining sum is1. This proves the boundary identity on every string, therefore on every vector, with finite support by integrability. All coefficients are in A, and E^(k) preserves the actual U_A module lattice, yielding the claimed generation. This reproduces Kashiwara91 Lemma6.1.4 and Proposition6.1.3 with a local proof of the finite Gaussian identity instead of importing Andrews' identity.

items.title: The Drinfeld pairing is nondegenerate in each root degree and matches the shuffle pairing
items.statement: The normalized D pairing is homogeneous, descends to the actual Serre halves and is nondegenerate/perfect over Q(q) in every finite root degree. Its rank-one values are those of the preceding Definition, with the factor(q_i−q_i^-1)^−n. It equals the formal generic Hopf pairing on the simple-root Borels with that exact generator and toral normalization. Thus D(xx′,y)=ΣD(x,y_(1))D(x′,y_(2)) and D(x,yy′)=ΣD(x_(1),y)D(x_(2),y′), with Δy on the negative Borel and Δ^opx on the positive Borel, including their toral factors. These are field identities; divided-power integral perfectness or A-valuedness is not asserted.
items.strategy: Transport through ι and multiply by the nonzero scalar d_nu^-1; the already-proved finite-dimensional homogeneous B_K form is nondegenerate, so D is perfect. Quotient descent follows directly from the actual half form; no free-word radical fallback is introduced. For Hopf matching, compare the formal generic pairing's generator/counit/toral values to this normalization. Extracting one E_i or F_i from its coproduct gives exactly the normalized skew recursion of B_K, with degree factor d_(nu)/d_(nu−alpha_i)=q_i−q_i^-1; word-height induction therefore identifies both pairings. The formal generic pairing supplies the consistent Borel extension, whose toral factors must be retained in the adjunction formulas. This verifies the field convention rather than asking an author to guess scalar twists.

items.statement: For a field basis u_a of U^+_nu and its D-dual basis v_a of U^-_-nu, the tensor Θ_nu=Σ_a u_a⊗v_a is independent of the chosen basis and Θ_0=1. It has finite-dimensional components and defines a vectorwise finite action under the exact root-height finiteness hypotheses of the completion Definition. Its degree-nu action shifts the label pair (mu,eta) to(mu+nu,eta−nu), preserving total weight. On finite-weight O_int pairs each fixed total-weight space has a uniform finite tail bound. No integral algebra coefficients are asserted; the positive-height components have no same-weight-pair diagonal term.
items.strategy: Changing the positive basis by an invertible finite field matrix changes its dual by the inverse transpose, so the sum is unchanged. The completion Definition proves the finite root set for each vector and the stronger uniform bound on a finite total-weight space. Degree shifts are immediate from the homogeneous root actions. This coevaluation statement is over Q(q), independent of lattice freeness or an A-perfect pairing.

items.title: The string-ideal triples are balanced: the induction step (Kashiwara 7.4.1 / JKK 10.4)
items.statement: Fix a root degree alpha of height r. Assume integral balanced/global lifts in every degree of height<r for both the negative half and all dominant highest modules, including based-quotient compatibility there and the negative-half string-ideal membership of each lower lift G∞(b) whenever b∈f̃_i^nB∞. Then for every i,n≥1 the image string-ideal J_(i,n)^A in each highest module, with its rational zero/infinity chart intersections, is integrally balanced in degree lambda−alpha. Its balanced Z-intersection maps isomorphically to the Z-span of Bλ∩f̃_i^n Bλ in that degree. Similarly the half ideal I_(i,n)^A is integrally balanced in degree−alpha, with residue Z-span B∞∩f̃_i^n B∞. Their Laurent extensions are free A-modules with these adapted global lifts. Freeness, chart intersection and the eventual module saturation J_(i,n)^A=V_A∩F_i^n V are conclusions, not hypotheses.
items.strategy:
Use the exact printed Kashiwara91 Proposition7.4.1, descending on n in the fixed degree, where n beyond the degree is zero. Assume J_(i,n+1)^A balanced. Put mu=lambda−alpha. If n+mu(h_i)<0, the boundary generation identity of the preceding supplier gives J_(i,−mu(h_i))^A_mu=V_A_mu, hence J_(i,n)^A_mu is the same full component as the already handled larger-n ideal. The field string-position sets agree because every admissible position at mu is at least−mu(h_i). Thus reduce to n+mu(h_i)≥0.
By definition J_n=F_i^(n)V_A[mu+n alpha_i]+J_(n+1). The lower-degree based quotient expresses the source V_A component using lower G∞(b) with surviving pi_lambda(b). If ẽ_i b≠0, lower-height negative-half string membership puts G∞(b) in I_(i,1)^A, so F_i^(n)G∞(b) lies in I_(i,n+1)^A by multiplying divided powers (integer Gaussians). It contributes only to J_(n+1). The remaining finite Z-module F is generated by phi_b=F_i^(n)G∞(b)v_lambda for ẽ_i b=0 and surviving image; their lower degree global lifts are bar fixed. To see phi_b∈L_mu+J_(n+1), extract P_iG∞(b): G∞(b)−P_iG∞(b) lies in F_iU^- with integral string coefficients, so its F_i^(n) multiple is in the image J_(n+1). The vector F_i^(n)P_iG∞(b) lies in L∞ and has residue f̃_i^n b, since lower-height string extraction and ẽ_i b=0 make all positive components of G∞(b) q-divisible. Project it to Llambda using the completed grand loop. Bar-fixedness of phi_b and bar stability of J_(n+1) give the analogous infinity condition.
The condition n+mu(h_i)≥0 ensures the module string at the surviving top class has length at least n; thus f̃_i^n pi(b) is nonzero and at exactly positionn. These classes biject onto (Bλ∩f̃_i^nBλ)\(f̃_i^(n+1)Bλ), using the completed crystal partial inverses and based quotient in lower degree. By descending balancedness, QJ_(n+1) has residue basis the higher positions, so phi(F) maps injectively modulo that rational subspace at0. The infinity injection is its bar image. Apply the correctly stated integral chart-extension lemma to M=J_n, N=J_(n+1), F with these explicit lifts. It proves balancedness, the exact integral residue sequence and the Z-basis consisting of the new n positions plus all higher positions. This also proves finite A-freeness as a conclusion.
For the half, choose all dominant coordinates large in the explicit auxiliary regular datum. In the fixed degree the Serre ideal is absent, so pi is a field isomorphism, and by definition carries U_A^- onto V_A, and I_n onto J_n. Grand-loop projection carries the rational zero chart isomorphically; commuting bar carries the infinity chart. Transport the already proved integral module triple and its signed-free residue basis back. No global half basis or module-saturation equality was assumed. This uses the primitive-coroot auxiliary weights exactly where the printed source requires large lambda.

items.title: The highest weight and negative half integral crystal triples are balanced
items.statement:
For every symmetrizable datum in the explicitly chosen label-weight category, the triples (U_A^-,L∞,bar L∞) and (V_A(lambda),Llambda,bar Llambda) are integrally balanced componentwise. Their balanced Z-intersections map isomorphically to ZB∞ and ZBλ, respectively; after rational extension these maps identify with the full Q crystal spaces. The inverse lifts G∞(b),Gλ(b) are bar invariant. They form actual A=Z[q,q^-1] bases of the divided-power modules U_A^- and V_A(lambda), with finite free root/label components of ranks equal to their field dimensions (the half ranks are the classical PBW ranks).
For every i,n≥1, I_(i,n)^A=⊕_(b∈B∞∩f̃_i^nB∞)A G∞(b), and J_(i,n)^A=⊕_(b∈Bλ∩f̃_i^nBλ)A Gλ(b). In particular the module image ideal equals V_A∩F_i^n V; this saturation follows from the adapted global basis and is not an initial hypothesis. Under pi_lambda, G∞(b) maps to0 exactly when its crystal image is0 and otherwise to Gλ(pi(b)). All assertions are integral, general symmetrizable and proved without an integral-freeness premise. If ẽ_i b=0 and n≥1, then G∞(f̃_i^n b)−F_i^(n)G∞(b) lies in I_(i,n+1)^A. This is the exact normalized top-string transition modulo the higher string ideal, not merely a modulo-q congruence.
items.strategy:
Induct simultaneously on root height r on the following exact statements: X, integral balancedness and based lifts of U_A^-; Y, integral balancedness and based lifts of every V_A(lambda); Z, negative-half global string-ideal membership. Carry lower-degree based-quotient zero/survival compatibility as a derived clause, used in the next height's module string step. Height0 has balanced intersection Z·1 or Z·v, integral residue Z and Laurent extension A, not Q. The already-proved grand loop supplies rational crystals; the separate integral-residue supplier supplies ZB∞. When auxiliary large/fundamental weights are used, first work in the explicit primitive-coroot regular datum and transport labels back.
At height r, the complete string-ideal induction supplier proves integral balancedness of every J_(i,n) and I_(i,n), with adapted free integral residue bases. Each new string lift is bar fixed: the ideal is generated over A by bar-fixed divided-word vectors, so for any lift g its difference g−bar g is divisible by q−q^-1 within the same integral ideal (write a finite divided-word expression and divide each antisymmetric Laurent coefficient). Its quotient lies in qL at0 because (q−q^-1)^-1 is in qA0, and lies in the infinity chart because g,bar g do; integral balanced injectivity on the ideal forces that quotient0. Thus each lift is fixed, without assuming the full height-r triple balanced.
For b∈f̃_iB∞∩f̃_jB∞ at degree−alpha, denote its two string lifts G_i(b),G_j(b). Write b as a lowering word with rightmost color k. Choose a dominant auxiliary lambda with lambda(h_k)=0 and all other coordinates greater than the degree bounds. The Serre quotient has kernel in this degree exactly U^-F_k, since every other singular generator has higher root degree. The crystal word kills the highest vector because its first executed lowering color is k. Each G_i(b)v lies in the corresponding integral module string ideal, in qLlambda and in bar Llambda; ideal balancedness forces it0. Likewise G_j(b)v=0. Hence their difference Q lies in U_A^-∩U^-F_k∩qL∞∩bar L∞. The local reversal supplier puts Qstar in U_A^-∩F_kU^-∩qL∞∩bar L∞. The already proved ordinary-power integral string extraction identifies U_A^-∩F_kU^-=I_(k,1)^A BEFORE this gluing step: the unique field position0 is zero and every extracted positive top coefficient is integral. Therefore Qstar is in I_(k,1)^A∩qL∞∩bar L∞, which is0 by the height-r string-ideal balance. Thus Q=0. This is the actual printed Kashiwara91 Lemma7.5.1 gluing argument, including its right-ideal/kernel and signed-star hypotheses.
Every positive-height crystal word has a lowering predecessor. Define G∞(b) by any available string lift; gluing makes it independent. Since U_A^- in this degree is Σ_i I_(i,1)^A (each divided-word generator has a first negative color), the free string-ideal bases give U_A^-=A·Σ_b ZG∞(b). These lifts inject into both rational chart residues: at0 they give the basis b, and at infinity their bar invariance gives the corresponding bar basis. Apply the integral chart generation lemma with the finite free Z-module F=ΣZG∞(b). It gives balancedness, the Z-balanced intersection, the A-basis and both chart bases. Each I_(i,n) lift now equals the full G∞ lift by uniqueness, proving its adapted basis and Z membership.
For a module, if pi(b)=0 choose i with ẽ_i b≠0. Its half lift lies in I_(i,1), so G∞(b)v lies in J_(i,1), qLlambda and bar Llambda; the already proved module ideal balance forces it0 (Kashiwara91 Lemma7.5.2). Surviving images are bar fixed, have residue pi(b), and these residues biject onto Bλ by the completed grand loop. They span V_A because pi(U_A^-)=V_A and the killed images are0. The finite free Z-span of surviving images injects into both rational residues; the chart generation lemma gives module balancedness and its actual A-basis. Uniqueness identifies these images with Gλ. Ideal lifts then agree with the corresponding module Gλ; their field scalar extensions span precisely F_i^n V. The direct free decomposition of V_A by all Gλ therefore proves J_(i,n)=V_A∩F_i^n V as a conclusion. This also proves the integral module residue subgroup is ZBλ.
The induction closes in every finite component. Global direct sums give integral bases with field ranks, and the published generic/classical half-rank supplier identifies the PBW ranks, carrying its existing AC hypothesis. No dot-U basis, rational-Q PID proof, false A-module residue, arbitrary torsionfree-to-free assertion, or chart containment assumption is used. The top-string transition is part of the integral chart extension step: its new residue lift is obtained from phi_b=F_i^(n)G∞(b) by subtracting an element of the higher ideal N=I_(i,n+1)^A to put it in both charts. The resulting integral balanced lift is uniquely G∞(f̃_i^n b). Thus their difference is in N exactly. The same fact holds in every module string image. This explicit transition supplies the signed-basis positive-recursion dictionary used by the canonical comparison.

items.title: Existence and uniqueness of the weightwise quasi-$R$ intertwiner
items.statement:
The D-coevaluation family Θ=Σ_nu Θ_nu∈∏U^+_nu⊗U^-_-nu is the unique normalized bar-coproduct intertwiner for the fixed Δ: Δ(u)Θ=Θ barΔ(u) for all u, where barΔ(u)=(psi⊗psi)Δ(psi(u)). It has Θ_0=1. Its generator recursions are
[1⊗E_i,Θ_nu]=Θ_(nu−alpha_i)(E_i⊗K_i)−(E_i⊗K_i^-1)Θ_(nu−alpha_i),
[F_i⊗1,Θ_nu]=Θ_(nu−alpha_i)(K_i^-1⊗F_i)−(K_i⊗F_i)Θ_(nu−alpha_i),
with negative-degree components0 and toral weight-zero commutation. In rank one Θ_n= (q_i−q_i^-1)^n[n]_(q_i²)! E_i^(n)⊗F_i^(n), so Θ_alpha_i=(q_i−q_i^-1)E_i⊗F_i. The family evaluates precisely under the completion's explicit finite-support hypotheses. This is not the native unscaled doubled-torus ΨΔ^op relation and no integral algebra coefficient claim is made.
items.strategy: Use the full printed Lusztig4.1.2 proof in the exact local normalization map. Its source Θ_L components use the B_L coevaluation with scalar(−1)^height ∏v_i^nu_i. The proved presentation map carries Δ_L to Δ^op and bar compatibly; tensor flip therefore carries its generator identity to ΔuΘ=ΘbarΔu. The degree-color computation already proves its tensors are exactly the D-coevaluation. To reproduce the actual source proof locally, expand Θ_nu in any homogeneous half bases with an unknown coefficient matrix. Commuting E_i/F_i through the opposite half uses the two skew derivations from the defining Serre presentation, a word-induction identity: the toral numerators contain left/right skew derivatives and denominator q_i−q_i^-1. Pair the remaining tensor factor with each basis vector; the two coevaluation expansion identities turn the four resulting derivative equations into the defining coproduct adjunction equations of D. Thus the prescribed coefficient matrix solves all generator equations, including both toral numerator coefficients, not a guessed single projector equation. In the difference of two normalized solutions, take minimal positive height. The lower terms in the derivative equations are0, forcing every coefficient vector in a positive-degree half to have all skew derivatives0. The established separation supplier makes it0. Pairing with every basis vector then kills the entire coefficient matrix, proving uniqueness by height induction. Multiplicativity extends generator equations to all u. Directly extracting homogeneous degree gives the two displayed commutator recursions; their first degree fixes the coefficient q_i−q_i^-1. Rank-one inversion of the stated D divided norm gives the displayed full Gaussian coefficient. This closes the field convention gap without importing an unproved dictionary from a doubled torus.

items.title: The quasi-$R$ intertwiner determines its inverse and the coproduct factorizations
items.statement:
In the same positive-first/negative-second completion, Θ^-1=barΘ=(psi⊗psi)(Θ). For every nu the exact threefold identities are
(Δ⊗id)Θ_nu=Σ_(gamma+eta=nu)(Θ_gamma)_23(1⊗K_-eta⊗1)(Θ_eta)_13,
(id⊗Δ)Θ_nu=Σ_(gamma+eta=nu)(Θ_gamma)_12(1⊗K_eta⊗1)(Θ_eta)_13.
The two normalized tensor-bar compositions satisfy the field cocycle identity ((Δ⊗id)Θ)Θ_12=((id⊗Δ)Θ)Θ_23, coefficientwise in the transported source completion and on every vector for which the iterated actions are finite. The inverse does not switch positive/negative tensor order. Removing Θ_0=1 permits scalar multiples of the same linear intertwiner equation, so normalization is essential. No integrality or uncontrolled infinite evaluation is asserted. The bar-coproduct counterpart needed for the cocycle is (id⊗barΔ)Θ_nu=Σ_(gamma+eta=nu)(Θ_gamma)_13(1⊗K_-gamma⊗1)(Θ_eta)_12.
items.strategy:
The bar of the intertwining equation gives barΔu·barΘ=barΘ·Δu. The product ΘbarΘ has zero component1 and commutes with ΔU. Equivalently the inverse, recursively defined in the positive root-height convolution algebra from Θ_0=1, has bar of itself satisfying the same normalized intertwiner equations as Θ. The established uniqueness therefore identifies the inverse with barΘ, exactly Lusztig4.1.3. No inverse in an opposite tensor completion is invented.
For the coproduct identities, follow the complete printed4.2.2 computation: expand the twisted half coproduct r(b)=Σ f(b,b1,b2)b1⊗b2 and its bar version, expand each coevaluation, and pair against arbitrary homogeneous basis tensors. Multiplication/coproduct adjunction of the half form identifies the paired coefficients with those of b1b2; the bar-twisted coproduct coefficient relation from§1.2.11 reverses their order with the precise root q-power. Toral commutation converts that power to K_±eta in the MIDDLE factor. Under v=q^-1, K_L↦K_K^-1 and threefold tensor reversal, the source4.2.2(a,b) give exactly the displayed orders/indices; at degree alpha_i they read ΔE_i⊗F_i and E_i⊗ΔF_i, fixing the indices. This pairing against a finite tensor basis is a complete degreewise proof.
The full source4.2.3 applies Δ to ΘbarΘ=1 and uses the paired coproduct expansions to obtain (id⊗barΔ)Θ_nu=Σ_(b+c=nu)Θ_b13 K_-b^(2) Θ_c12, with K^(2) in the middle tensor position, after the exact convention map. Now the LEFT cocycle expression ((Δ⊗id)Θ)Θ12 expands by the already-proved Δ identity as Σ_(a,b,c)Θ_a23 K_-b^(2) Θ_b13 Θ_c12. The RIGHT expression ((id⊗Δ)Θ)Θ23 equals Θ23((id⊗barΔ)Θ), by intertwining applied in positions23 to every negative-half coefficient. The counterpart identity expands it as Σ_(a,b,c)Θ_a23 Θ_b13 K_-b^(2) Θ_c12. These expressions are identical because a middle-position K commutes with Θ_b13. For fixed outer root degrees, b+c and a+b are fixed, so the possible a,b,c form a finite set; the coefficient calculation involves no uncontrolled infinite rearrangement. This is the complete transported4.2.4 argument and proves field parenthesization independently of integral action. In the highest-module setting the same identity can be checked without formal manipulation: both composite bars are U-compatible, agree on v_lambda⊗m⊗n (the first highest kills all positive root terms), and induction on the first negative divided-word height using ΔF^(r)'s coefficient1 term forces agreement everywhere. Finiteness is verified before evaluating any completed identity. Finally, the linear intertwining equations are homogeneous, so scaling Θ scales its zero component and gives precisely the claimed unnormalized family.

items.statement: For U^- and every dominant V(lambda), there exists a unique lower global family G(b)⊂M_A∩L∩bar L with residue b. items.title: The upper (form-dual) global basis and the required perfectness of the integral pairing
items.statement:
Let M=⊕_mu M_mu be U^- or V(lambda), with finite root/label components, lower global A-lattice M_A=⊕_b A G(b), rational lower charts L0 and L∞=bar L0, and the normalized homogeneous Kashiwara half or highest-module polarization B. Define its RESTRICTED graded integral form-dual by M_A^vee=⊕_mu{x∈M_mu:B(x,(M_A)_mu)⊂A}. Define dual rational charts L0^vee={x:B(x,L0)⊂A0} and L∞^vee={x:B(x,L∞)⊂A∞}, also as restricted direct sums. The upper global family is the unique homogeneous field family G^up(b) with B(G(b′),G^up(b))=delta_(b,b′). Its existence and actual dual-lattice bases/perfection are proved by the next theorem.
The upper bar is the B-adjoint semilinear involution psi^vee determined by B(psi u,psi^vee v)=overline{B(u,v)}. Upper Kashiwara operators are ẽ_i^up=(f̃_i^low)^adj and f̃_i^up=(ẽ_i^low)^adj, defined componentwise by the nondegenerate finite-dimensional form. They are distinct from the lower operators in general. The upper zero chart is the dual chart L0^vee; post-grand-loop perfection identifies it with L0, but the upper infinity chart L∞^vee is not automatically the lower bar chart L∞. The exact assertions of the following theorem are weightwise perfect A-duality, dual globalization in these genuine dual charts, and crystal compatibility for the respective adjoint operators. No full product Hom_A(M_A,A) identification, lower A-self-duality, ordinary-bar fixedness or unqualified upper/lower operator equality is asserted.
items.strategy: Each homogeneous field form is nondegenerate in finite dimension, so adjoints and the homogeneous dual vectors are defined by ordinary inverse Gram linear algebra over Q(q). The restricted direct sum is necessary for infinite-rank U^- and infinite-dimensional integrable modules: the ordinary full algebraic dual would be a product. The dual charts use their own coefficient rings, not the lower infinity chart by fiat. The semilinear adjoint bar exists uniquely from finite nondegeneracy; applying its defining equality twice proves its square is1. Adjoints of the lower string shifts have the explicitly weighted divided-string formulas supplied next, so this Definition hides no exact unweighted adjunction or integral-lattice perfectness assumption.

items.title: The based quotient: projection of the lower global basis to a highest weight module
items.statement: The projection pi_lambda:U_A^-→V_A(lambda) is a based quotient over Z[q,q^-1]: G∞(b) maps to0 if its crystal image is0 and to Gλ(pi(b)) otherwise. Thus its kernel is the A-span of exactly the killed global basis elements, and the surviving global basis elements map bijectively onto the integral highest-module basis. The module weight components are finite free over A, and the compatible zero/infinity chart and residue projections have the already proved crystal compatibility. This holds for every symmetrizable datum with the explicit label/auxiliary-realization convention. More precisely its integral kernel is Σ_iΣ_(s>lambda(h_i)) U_A^-F_i^(s). Thus the integral highest-module presentation uses ALL divided right powers beyond each highest limit, not just an ordinary power with a nonunit factorial.
items.strategy: Apply the integral balanced theorem’s actual string-ideal argument for killed images and its uniqueness argument for surviving images. The free A-decompositions then make the kernel precisely the span of killed basis vectors and give the quotient basis, with no appeal to symmetric canonical-basis agreement. Chart projection and modulo-q compatibility come from the completed grand loop and commuting bar. This is Kashiwara91 Lemma7.5.2 and the final proof of Theorem7(ii), printed p.516, not an unproved quotient fallback. For this integral presentation, reversal preserves integral/chart lattices and carries each global lift to a signed global lift: its image is bar fixed, its integral residue has norm1, hence is ±a crystal residue, and balanced uniqueness supplies the signed lift. It therefore carries the already saturated left ideal I_(i,n)^A to the saturated right ideal R_(i,n)^A=U_A^-∩U^-F_i^n=Σ_(s≥n)U_A^-F_i^(s), each adapted to subsets of one signed global basis. The field Serre kernel is Σ_iU^-F_i^(lambda(h_i)+1). A sum of subspaces spanned by subsets of one basis is the span of their union; intersecting its field span with the full free A-global lattice gives exactly the A-span of that union. This proves the stated integral sum of all divided right ideals, without presuming that arbitrary integral intersections commute with sums.

items.statement: Assume AC only for the generic/classical PBW rank supplier. Over A=Z[q,q^-1], multiplication U_A^-⊗_A U_A^0⊗_A U_A^+→U_A is an isomorphism. The two divided-power halves are free A-modules with finite free root components of the classical PBW ranks. The unmodified torus has an A-basis K_c∏K_i^{delta_i}T_{i,0,t_i}, with delta_i=0 or1 and c representing Pvee/Σ Z(d_i h_i). Hence U_A is free, and the degree-beta component is ⊕_{alpha,gamma∈Q_+, alpha-gamma=beta} U_A^-[-gamma]⊗U_A^0⊗U_A^+[alpha]. Unique coefficients refer to products of chosen basis elements, not to arbitrary sums of simple tensors.
items.strategy: Apply the simultaneous integral balanced/global construction (Kashiwara91 Sections6.1 and7.1-7.5) to U_A^-. That construction starts with an arbitrary Z[q±]-submodule and rational DVR-free chart lattices; its integral residue and height/string-ideal argument proves the actual A-basis as a conclusion. Use its negative-half global basis in each finite root degree. The unmodified integral toral-basis lemma independently supplies the full K_coset ∏K_i^delta_iT_{i,0,t_i} A-basis by Gaussian Vandermonde, toral shift/action recursions and Laurent-extremal independence. Both factors are genuinely free over the non-PID A; their tensor product with the positive half is free. Reordering gives the multiplication surjection; tensoring a kernel with Q(q) gives zero by field triangular decomposition, and the free source has no torsion, so the kernel is zero. Its homogeneous restriction gives the negative-toral-positive root decomposition. Extension to Q(q) and the published generic/classical comparison give the claimed component ranks, with AC used only in that rank supplier. No torsionfree-to-free claim over A and no modified dot-U basis is used.

items.title: Specialization of the global bases and the root-of-unity boundary
items.statement:
For every dominant lambda, the integral highest lattice V_A(lambda) has its genuine lower global A-basis. Hence for ANY unital base change A→S, including nonflat q=ζ specializations with ζ invertible, its tensor fibre has the corresponding S-basis and identical finite weight ranks. At characteristic-zero q=1 the positive toral quotient and local comparison identify it with the classical simple integrable highest module and its Weyl–Kac character.
The zero/infinity CHART lattices are obtained separately from Z[q]- and Z[q^-1]-spans of the global vectors, then rational DVR extension; there is no map A→A0 sending the unit q to0. At roots of unity the free integral fibre basis still survives, but this does not assert simplicity or semisimplicity, or equality with a naive ordinary-generator specialization. If the order of ζ_i² is greater than1, its Gaussian factorial vanishes once the index reaches that order; at ζ_i²=1 in characteristic0 it has value r! and that particular vanishing argument does not apply. Thus the algebra/module root-of-unity boundary is distinguished from the unconditional free-basis base-change fact.
items.strategy: A direct sum of free A-basis vectors tensors to the corresponding free S-basis for every unital A-algebra S; flatness and injectivity are unnecessary. The q=1 module comparison is the proved local/global highest-module theorem and exact positive toral quotient, preserving every weight rank and the classical character. The integral balanced chart factorization uses Z[q]G or Z[q^-1]G before localizing at0 or infinity; q is a unit in A and cannot be specialized to0 there. At root-of-unity values use [r]_(ζ_i²)!=∏_(j=1)^r(1+ζ_i²+...+ζ_i^(2(j−1))). If ζ_i² has order l>1 its l-th factor is0; if it is1 each factor isj. These exact scalar computations show why ordinary divided-generator identification can fail, while the genuine integral basis itself still base changes. No unsupported root-of-unity simplicity theorem is imported.

items.title: Lusztig's canonical basis and Kashiwara's lower global basis agree in symmetric type
items.statement: In symmetric finite ADE type (all d_i=1), transport Lusztig's parameter by v=q^-1, the abstract half generators θ_i^(n)↦F_i^(n), and full torus K_h^L↦K_(-h). Divided-power integral forms and bar agree under this transport; the half forms agree by B_L=C_nu B_K, not by an unqualified identity. Under this exact dictionary Lusztig's canonical LOWER basis equals the Kashiwara lower global basis of U^-, and its canonical highest-module quotient bases equal the corresponding lower global bases for every dominant label lambda (using the explicit regular realization). The signed canonical set equals ±G∞; the positive canonical choice is matched by its actual Ti,n top-string recursion. No equality of upper and lower bases, or unproved 'unitriangular word-basis' characterization, is asserted.
items.strategy:
Use the proved full form/parameter/coproduction dictionary. The actual source14.2.3/14.2.4 defines the canonical signed set as integral bar-fixed elements x with B_L(x,x)∈1+qZ[[q]] after v=q^-1. Every G∞ is integral/bar fixed and lies in L∞; the Kashiwara residue pairing is orthonormal and its integral values lie in A_Z⊂Z[[q]], while C_nu is a unit≡1 with integer power series. Thus ±G∞ satisfies the signed norm condition. Conversely that norm condition and C_nu unit imply B_K(x,x)∈A0; the already-proved norm criterion puts x in L∞. Bar-fixedness puts it in bar L∞ too. Integral globalization therefore writes x as a finite Z-combination of the lower G∞. Its norm residue is a positive sum of integer squares1, so x=±G∞. This proves the entire signed-basis characterization locally rather than importing its geometric existence proof.
The source14.3.2 defines Bi;n by the left string ideals and Ti,n by the UNIQUE signed element b′ of exact string positionn such that F_i^(n)b−b′ is an integral linear combination of strictly higher string positions. The already-proved adapted global ideal bases identify this signed partition with the crystal epsilon partition. The explicit top-string transition from integral globalization gives Ti,n(G∞(b))=G∞(f̃_i^n b) when ẽ_i b=0. The sign is+1, fixed by that exact coefficient1 quotient relation. Source14.4.2 defines the positive canonical basis recursively from1 by these Ti,n transitions. The positive Kashiwara crystal has precisely the same recursion: every positive-height b has some epsilon_i=n>0, with top ẽ_i^n b in smaller height, and b=f̃_i^n(ẽ_i^n b). Induction on height therefore identifies the positive source canonical basis with G∞, eliminating the signed ambiguity. This verifies the positive construction, not just their almost-orthonormal norms or names.
Source14.4.11–14.4.12 defines the highest-module canonical basis by the based quotient of the half, with killed right-string-ideal elements omitted. The completed local based-quotient theorem gives exactly the same zero/survival formula on G∞. The full parameter/torus map preserves the highest character: K_h^L acts by v^<h,lambda>=q^(-<h,lambda>), the eigenvalue of K_(-h) on the library highest module. The early auxiliary regular datum discharges the source Y-regularity and transports the original label weights back. Hence these quotient bases coincide. This argument preserves the approved ADE conclusion without using upper-duality or identifying upper vectors with lower ones.

items.title: Finitely generated free integral weight lattices and deformation of the classical weight character
items.statement: For every dominant label weight lambda, let V_A=U_Av_lambda=U_A^-v_lambda inside the simple integrable L(lambda). Over A=Z[q,q^-1], each label-weight component of V_A is finite FREE of rank dim_Q(q)L(lambda)_mu, not merely torsionfree. It spans the field module. For every characteristic-zero q=1 specialization k, the fibre has the same weight dimensions and is the classical simple integrable highest module of the explicitly regularized realization, transported to the original label lattice. Thus its character is the Weyl-Kac character (the finite Weyl character in finite type). The integral Serre quotient equals L(lambda) in every symmetrizable type, as already proved by the early local comparison.
items.strategy: The simultaneous global construction and its based-quotient theorem give a Z[q±]-basis of U_A^-v_lambda: each negative global basis element maps to the corresponding highest-module global element if its crystal image survives, and to0 otherwise (Kashiwara91 Theorem7(ii), Section7.5.2). Thus each finite weight lattice is actually free over A, with rank its field dimension. The early local-q1 deformation/universality theorem already proves the simple quantum module, field character and equality with the integrable Serre quotient using DVR-free lattices; it is not dependent on this global result. Base change of the newly proved integral weight basis preserves dimensions. Algebraic positive specialization and finite-support regularization identify the classical fibre and its character, and the classical Weyl-Kac theorem gives the explicit formula. Perfect-pairing/regularity/fundamental-weight hypotheses used by the sources are established by the actual auxiliary-datum lemma. This proves the stronger original global Z-lattice assertion without assuming it as a balanced-triple premise.

items.title: Upper and lower global bases are dual and crystal compatible
items.statement:
For every finite root/label component of M=U^- or V(lambda), the restricted integral dual M_A^vee has the actual A-basis {G^up(b)} dual to {G(b)}, and B:(M_A^vee)_mu×(M_A)_mu→A is perfect. Globally these bases form direct sums; this means restricted graded perfectness, not identification with the full product Hom_A(M_A,A).
The dual charts are L0^vee=⊕A0G^up(b) and L∞^vee=⊕A∞G^up(b), and their balanced Z-intersection is ⊕ZG^up(b). Thus the dual triple is integrally balanced. At0, L0^vee=L0 and G^up(b) has residue b; at infinity its residue is the dual of the lower infinity-chart class in the dual infinity chart. The upper bar psi^vee fixes each G^up(b). The upper operators satisfy EXACT mixed adjunction B(f̃^low u,v)=B(u,ẽ^up v), B(ẽ^low u,v)=B(u,f̃^up v). Their reductions at0 equal the lower crystal operators and give the same crystal set B.
For a divided module string F_i^(n)v of top rank-one weight a, put d_(a,n)=q_i^(n(a−n))[a choose n]_i. Then ẽ_i^up at position n≥1 multiplies the preceding divided position by d_(a,n)/d_(a,n−1)=q_i^(a−2n+1)[a−n+1]_i/[n]_i, and f̃_i^up at position n<a multiplies the next by its reciprocal d_(a,n)/d_(a,n+1). For a half string with e_i′v=0, put d_n=q_i^(−n(n−1)/2)/[n]_i!=1/[n]_(q_i²)!; the corresponding ratios are d_n/d_(n−1)=1/[n]_(q_i²) and d_n/d_(n+1)=[n+1]_(q_i²). All admissible ratios are units≡1 in A0. Consequently unweighted lower adjunction holds modulo q, but generally not exactly over Q(q). No equality of upper and lower integral bases, even in symmetric type, is implied.
items.strategy:
Fix a finite component and its already-proved lower A-basis g_b=G(b). The field Gram matrix C=(B(g_b,g_c)) is invertible over Q(q), not asserted invertible over A. Define g_b^up using C^-1. For any x in the component, its coordinates in this dual field basis are exactly B(g_b,x). Hence x is in M_A^vee iff those coordinates are in A. This proves its genuine free A-basis and the perfect pairing with M_A, by the evaluation matrices delta; no A-unit determinant or lower self-duality is required. This is a finite proof in each degree, extended only by restricted direct sums.
The lower chart lattices have bases g_b over A0 and A∞ by integral globalization. The same coefficient criterion proves their dual chart bases g_b^up over the corresponding rings. Their triple intersection is Z-span because A∩A0∩A∞=Z. The exact integral dual globalization follows, with Q extension at each rational residue. Existing post-grand-loop Gram perfection identifies L0^vee=L0, and B(g_b,g_c)≡delta at0 implies g_b^up≡b there. At infinity, pairing with the lower infinity basis defines the actual dual residue; it does not assert congruence modulo q^-1 in the LOWER infinity lattice. Since psi g_b=g_b, the definition B(psi u,psi^vee v)=overline B(u,v) gives psi^vee g_b^up=g_b^up and transports the two dual charts.
For exact operators, extract finite divided strings. Different positions with different highest components are orthogonal: repeated E_i or e_i′ adjunction leaves a highest vector paired with a positive F_i power, hence0; at equal position the pairing is d_(a,n) or d_n times the top-component form. Therefore the adjoint of the normalized lower shift has precisely the displayed norm ratio, proving the exact MIXED adjunction. The module ratio equals (1−q_i^(2(a−n+1)))/(1−q_i^(2n)) after factoring powers, a unit with constant1 for 1≤n≤a. The half ratios are the displayed ordinary q_i² quantum integers and reciprocals, also units≡1. Thus the upper operators preserve L0, reduce to the same crystal actions and satisfy the same partial-inverse edge property. This is Kashiwara91§2.4’s distinction between lower and upper operators, combined with its§5.1 A0-perfection and the constructed global bases. No star-invariance argument is substituted for form-duality, no rank-one check is promoted to a general proof, and no full infinite-rank algebraic dual is invoked.

items.title: Divided-power integrality of the quasi-$R$ action on based lattices
items.statement:
For the actual Θ∈U^+⊗U^- and the exact four-axiom based modules, integral ACTION is proved in these cases: (a) V(lambda)⊗N for any based N (highest FIRST); (b) M⊗ωV(lambda) for any based M (lowest SECOND), with vectorwise finite action; (c) arbitrary U_A-stable based pairs in FINITE Cartan type; (d) a first factor in C_high with arbitrary based second, or an arbitrary based first with second in C_low, under vectorwise finite action. Here C_high consists of exact based subquotients of weight-admissible direct sums of finite highest tensor constructions; C_low is its lowest/unsigned-Chevalley counterpart. Based subobjects are saturated basis subsets and quotient maps are integral/bar compatible. These classes are closed under their normalized finite tensor construction. In particular all finite highest products and ordered highest-prefix/arbitrary-based-middle/lowest-suffix products have the integral tensor action and construction. Upper-cone/finite-component conditions are imposed on direct sums; in the lowest case use its explicit lower-cone action bound. No arbitrary based-O_int pair is covered in general type.
In these cases Θ preserves the actual integral tensor lattice and has A-valued ACTION coefficients in its tensor bases. Its degree0 component is identity; every positive root component shifts the first label up and second down, so the bar is locally weight-transfer triangular with diagonal1. In finite Cartan type the stronger algebra coefficients Θ_nu∈U_A^+_nu⊗U_A^-_-nu are also proved. That stronger universal coefficient claim is false in general affine type. A normalized triangular bar-correction constructs the genuine tensor global basis; raw tensor products of lower basis vectors need not themselves be bar fixed. The class in(d) means based subquotients of weight-admissible direct sums of finite highest tensors with the constructed tensor basis, not arbitrary integral lattices in semisimple field modules. The affine construction in the proof explicitly disproves unqualified arbitrary-based action integrality while retaining these full general symmetrizable cases.
items.strategy:
Highest-first action. The exact divided coproduct is ΔF_i^(r)=Σ_(t=0)^r q_i^(−t(r−t))F_i^(r−t)K_i^t⊗F_i^(t). This follows from q-commutation of F_i⊗1 and K_i⊗F_i and the finite Gaussian theorem. On a homogeneous m of label mu its t coefficient is q_i^(t(mu(h_i)−r+t)), an A-unit. The t=0 term is F_i^(r)m⊗n with coefficient1. The tensor bar Ψ=Θ(psi⊗psi) fixes v_lambda⊗b for each bar-fixed b of N, because every positive root kills the first top. Induct on the first divided-word height. Solve the displayed Δ expression for F_i^(r)m⊗n; all t>0 inputs have strictly smaller first height. U/bar compatibility of Ψ and bar stability of U_A make their barred outputs integral by induction. Thus Ψ preserves every pure divided-word tensor, hence V_A(lambda)⊗N_A, with termination at the finite word height and separately established Θ action finiteness. Since the factor bar is an A-bijection, Θ itself preserves that lattice. This is the complete Bao–Wang approximate-cyclicity proof in the flipped convention; neither lattice freeness nor a highest decomposition of N is used.
Lowest-second action is the exact dual induction: ΔE_i^(r)=Σ_t q_i^(t(r−t))E_i^(t)⊗K_i^-t E_i^(r−t), whose t=0 term raises only the second factor with coefficient1. Θ fixes b⊗the second lowest vector. Induct on its finite positive divided-word height, with t>0 smaller second height and U_A-stable first factor. The lower support bounds give finite action separately. The same reasoning applies to Verma-generated integral images when needed, not an arbitrary invented integral highest section.
Finite-type universal coefficients. Choose a longest Weyl element w0 and sufficiently large regular dominant weights. In each finite highest module construct its lowest extremal vector by the reduced w0 string of divided powers. Each step is a complete rank-one top-to-bottom string, whose normalized norm factor d_(a,a)=1; weights at the extrema are one-dimensional by the already-proved classical character comparison. Hence the extremal vector is integral, bar fixed, norm1, and is the unique signed global element at that weight by the established q0 norm/globalization criterion. Let ω be the unsigned E↔F,K↔K^-1 Chevalley map. It commutes with the normalized sigma (check generators with the toral q² factors), so the field isomorphism from the corresponding lowest module to the highest module, normalized at that extremal vector, is a form isometry and bar compatible. Its source integral lattice maps into the target because the extremal vector is integral and U_A stable. Every transported global vector is integral/bar fixed with residue norm1; the integral signed norm criterion identifies it with ±a target global basis vector. Equal finite dimensions prove a signed integral lattice identification: the transported basis is the target global basis up to individual signs. This is an A-basis/lattice identification, sufficient for the coefficient test below; it is not asserted to be a strict based morphism (which would require basis images without minus signs). Thus the integral lowest and highest lattices are genuinely identified, not merely their field spaces.
Expand Θ_nu in positive/negative global half bases with field coefficients. Choose the finite highest/lowest test modules large enough that all half basis elements in that degree survive their based projections; after the just-proved signed extremal lattice identification these actions are ±distinct global basis vectors. Apply Θ to the lowest extremal vector of the first highest module and the highest extremal vector of the second lowest module. Highest-first action already proves this output integral. Different degrees have distinct weight PAIRS, and in the fixed degree the output basis vectors are independent parts of an actual A-basis. Therefore every expansion coefficient is in A. This reproduces the actual source24.1.6 finite-type argument, including its w0/integral basis prerequisite. It proves algebra integrality in finite type only and hence integral action on arbitrary based pairs there.
General highest tensor construction and closure. Form right-associated products of highest modules: highest-first action proves integral bar at every step, while the field cocycle gives all parenthesizations the same bar without assuming integral action for intermediate arbitrary pairs. The partial order is the first-weight-up/second-weight-down transfer order (and its iterated prefix-weight version). Positive components give strictly transferred pairs, only Θ_0 gives diagonal1. Every relevant upward interval has finite root bounds; for highest/O_int factors each total-weight block is finite as well. In a finite interval solve for a bar-fixed lift g_t=e_t+Σ_(s>t)a_ts e_s with a_ts∈qZ[q], starting at its top. After subtracting already constructed larger lifts, involutivity makes the remaining coefficient f satisfy f+bar f=0. Its unique positive-q part a with a−bar a=f supplies the next correction. Finite induction gives existence/uniqueness and a unitriangular A-matrix with a finite-interval inverse. The corrected family is an A-basis, an A0-basis with the raw tensor crystal residues, and bar-fixed; its A∞-span is the ACTUAL tensor bar chart. Thus its integral balanced intersection is its Z-span. The completed crystal tensor rule supplies the lattice operators/residue basis; bar does not literally preserve A0. This is the full semilinear system proof of Lusztig24.2.1 and the Bao–Wang2.7/2.9 extension, reproduced locally.
For two such highest tensor objects P,Q, the cocycle identifies their grouped tensor bar with the integral normalized bar on the concatenated highest factors. The factor bars are A-bijections, so Θ on P⊗Q is integral. Based subobjects are spanned by subsets of their actual constructed bases and hence saturated: (P_A⊗Q_A)∩(P′⊗Q′)=P′_A⊗Q′_A. Θ preserves their field submodules by its U-monomial terms; integral action follows from that equality. Based quotient maps are U-linear, send basis to basis-or0, have a basis-subset kernel, and commute with bars because both bars fix those bases. Their integral tensor maps are surjective onto free complementary quotient lattices; Θ commutes with the maps termwise, so integral action descends. No field summand is converted into an integral section. Direct sums are handled componentwise with their stated finite weight/upper-cone bounds. These arguments establish exactly the admissible closure class stated above.
Affine algebra and ACTION boundaries. For A1^(1), a01=a10=−2, the degree-delta Kashiwara Gram in F0F1,F1F0 is [[1,q²],[q²,1]]. The correct D coevaluation has factor (q−q^-1)²/(1−q⁴)=q^-2(1−q²)/(1+q²), so it is not a universally integral algebra tensor. For the stronger arbitrary-pair failure, take dominant lambda=Lambda0, mu=lambda−delta and p=[2]. The global g=F1F0v_lambda satisfies E0g=0,E1g=pF0v; F0^(r)g=0 for r≥2 by the length-three divided Serre relation applied to the first highest vector, and F1g=pF1^(2)F0v,F1^(r)g=0 for r≥2 by its rank-one length2 string. The proved integral based-quotient presentation therefore gives a U_A-map V_A(mu)/p→V_A(lambda)/p, sending the highest vector to g modp. For each global h_b its image has bar-fixed coefficients in A/(p)=Z[i], whose bar-fixed ring is Z. Let T_b be its unique integer-coordinate lift in the lambda global basis. Define c_b=h_b+T_b/p and M_A with free basis B_lambda∪{c_b} inside Vlambda⊕Vmu. U_A-stability follows because U T_b−T(Uh_b) is divisible by p. All basis vectors are homogeneous/bar fixed; because 1/p=q/(1+q²)∈qA0, its EXACT chart/residue data equal the standard direct-sum based module, proving all four based axioms, not just field integrability. For N=Vmu and its highest h_mu, Θ(c_top⊗h_mu)=c_top⊗h_mu−(1−q²)/(1+q²)v_lambda⊗g_mu. The simple-root terms vanish; E0E1g=pv,E1E0g=0,F0F1h_mu=0,F1F0h_mu=g_mu, and every higher first raising degree vanishes. The displayed coefficient is not in A and is on a distinct tensor basis vector. Thus the original unrestricted arbitrary based-O_int ACTION assertion is false. The theorem's corrected ordered/constructed hypotheses are mathematically necessary, not a finite-type convenience restriction. For the stronger closure statement, first concatenate a pure highest product P with an arbitrary based N. Right-associated highest-first action makes the whole normalized bar integral. The field cocycle identifies it with the grouped bar Ψ_(P,N); since both factor bars are A-bijections, Θ preserves P_A⊗N_A. Repeat the exact basis-subset intersection and based-quotient image argument on the FIRST factor only, giving C_high⊗N without assuming N belongs to that class. The dual lowest-second argument gives M⊗C_low. Normalized tensor products of based morphisms remain based: they commute with bars and module crystal operators; their image of a tensor global element is integral/bar fixed with the corresponding raw tensor residue or0. The proved triangular balanced uniqueness forces the corresponding target global element or0, and the free bases make the kernel exactly the killed basis subset. Therefore subobjects/quotients of pure highest tensor parents remain based subquotients after further tensoring, proving closure of C_high; likewise C_low. For an ordered highest-prefix/based-middle/lowest-suffix product, each binary split has either a pure highest-class left block or a pure lowest-class right block, so the appropriate action case applies.
