items.title: Tensor bars on finite products of based integrable modules
items.statement:
For ANY finite sequence of based integrable modules in finite-weight-space O_int, the field tensor bar Ψ=Θ(composite factor bars) is well defined, semilinear, U/bar compatible, involutive and independent of all parenthesizations. All root-height sums are vectorwise finite. This field assertion is preserved for arbitrary based pairs; it does not imply integral action.
Its integral/based assertion holds for the actual admissible cases proved by the integral-action supplier: highest-first or first C_high with arbitrary based second; arbitrary based first with lowest/C_low second under finite action; all finite highest products and exact based subquotients/direct sums of their tensor constructions; ordered highest-prefix/based-middle/lowest-suffix products with explicit local support bounds; and arbitrary based pairs/products in finite Cartan type (including the finite-degree polynomial type-A modules). For any other pair the same conclusion is conditional on an independently PROVED integral Θ action, not field semisimplicity or lattice freeness.
In these cases Ψ preserves the divided-power integral tensor lattice. Its action on raw tensor lower basis vectors is locally weight-transfer triangular with diagonal1; the actual tensor global vectors are its uniquely corrected bar-fixed lifts congruent to those raw tensor vectors moduloq, with corrections in qZ[q]. They form a genuine A-basis and give the integral balanced tensor triple. The q0 tensor lattice and crystal basis are supplied separately by the completed crystal tensor rule. Its infinity chart is Ψ(L0_tensor), not an asserted bar containment in L0; semilinearity sends q toq^-1. The raw tensor lower vectors are generally not bar fixed. The exact based integral/bar-compatible subquotient maps preserve the corrected global bases by balanced uniqueness. No assertion covers arbitrary two-sided-unbounded evaluation, semi-infinite limits, a universal-R braiding, or general arbitrary-based integral action (the affine boundary in the supplier disproves the latter).
items.strategy:
Field construction first. Θ's explicit positive-first weight action is finite on upper-cone pairs and their finite products; on the ordered lowest cases use the supplied lower bounds before evaluating. Define the binary semilinear bar as Θ(psi_M⊗psi_N). Its scalar involution is q↦q^-1. Applying it twice gives ΘbarΘ=1, hence Ψ²=id. The exact ΔuΘ=ΘbarΔu gives Ψ(u x)=psi(u)Ψ(x). For three factors the two maps are ((Δ⊗id)Θ)Θ12 times factor bars and ((id⊗Δ)Θ)Θ23 times factor bars; the established field cocycle makes them equal. Binary associativity generates all finite rebracketings. This uses no integral action assumption and retains the valid rational theorem for arbitrary O_int inputs.
Integral cases are the complete action proof of the preceding supplier, not inferred from freeness or sourcefinite-type statements outside their range. With those hypotheses, Ψ preserves the A-tensor lattice and Ψ²=1 makes it an A-bijection. Each positive root term raises the first factor's label and lowers the second; only degree0 fixes a label pair, so it is triangular with diagonal1 in the explicit weight-transfer order. The supplier's finite semilinear correction algorithm then gives unique Ψ-fixed tensor global vectors with qZ[q] corrections. Local finite intervals ensure all corrections and inverse transition sums terminate. For upper-cone inputs each fixed total-weight block is finite; for ordered lowest suffixes use bounded transfer intervals instead of falsely claiming finite-dimensional mixed total-weight spaces.
The corrected vectors form an A-basis and an A0-basis of the ORIGINAL tensor crystal lattice; their residue classes are precisely the raw tensor crystal basis. Because they are Ψ-fixed, their A∞-span is the actual bar chart Ψ(L0_tensor). Intersecting the Laurent/zero/infinity coefficient rings in this basis gives Z-span and proves integral balancedness. Thus q0 crystal stability is a consequence of the independent crystal tensor supplier, whereas the bar chart is an infinity chart; no bar-preserves-A0 assertion is made. The integral tensor lattice is U_A-stable by the explicit Gaussian divided coproducts for E/F and diagonal toral Gaussian actions on the chosen label basis. Homogeneous corrected weights, U/bar compatibility and the residue tensor crystal verify every based condition. Exact based subobjects/quotients have saturated basis-subset kernels, commute with bar and residue operators; their images of these global lifts are integral/bar fixed with one residue or0, so balanced uniqueness proves basis-or0 compatibility. This proves the claimed inheritance without arbitrary integral sections.

items.title: Bar invariance and the congruence modulo $q$ do not imply balancedness
items.statement:
Bar-fixedness and a prescribed residue alone do not imply balancedness, global parametrization or uniqueness. First, in the two-dimensional sl2 module use L′=A0(v+w)⊕qA0v and its ACTUAL bar lattice A∞(v+w)⊕q^-1A∞v. With V_A=Av⊕Aw, its balanced part is Z(v+w), whose residue image misses the valid nonzero class qv+qL′. The vector v+w is bar fixed but L′ fails the crystal-lattice weight/stability axioms; it is a general-lattice failure of existence/parametrization, not by itself a uniqueness counterexample.
For a genuine separate nonuniqueness witness use the one-dimensional trivial module Q(q)v with integral lattice Av, bar v=v, and crystal lattice L″=q^-1A0v (all operators0) with bar L″=qA∞v. Its balanced intersection is Zq^-1v⊕Zv⊕Zqv, mapping onto the Z-residue generator q^-1v+qL″ with nonzero kernel. The two DISTINCT bar-fixed integral vectors (q+q^-1)v and(q+q^-1)v+v have the same nonzero crystal residue. Thus even a valid scaled crystal lattice plus bar invariance/congruence does not force unique global lifts without the actual balanced map. Neither example is the canonical top-normalized Kashiwara triple of a highest module.
items.strategy:
For L′ use a=v+w,t=v. Its integral zero intersection is Z[q]a⊕qZ[q]t; its infinity intersection is Z[q^-1]a⊕q^-1Z[q^-1]t, because bar sends qv toq^-1v. The triple intersection is Za, while the integral zero residue is Za⊕Zqv. This proves the missing qv class; v itself is not in L′, so v+qL′ is undefined and never asserted. The elementary ẽa=v and coefficient calculation show the lattice is free/full but not crystal stable or weight decomposed, distinguishing this failure from the next example.
In the trivial module all Kashiwara operators vanish; every homogeneous full free scaled A0 lattice is a genuine crystal lattice, and q^-1v is its residue basis representative. The simultaneous Laurent coefficient bounds for L″ and bar L″ are exponents−1≤k≤1, giving exactly the displayed rank3 Z intersection. Reducing modulo qL″=A0v kills v and qv but not q^-1v. Both proposed integral vectors are fixed by q↦q^-1, lie in the simultaneous intersection and have coefficient1 on q^-1v, hence the same nonzero crystal class; their difference v≠0 is in the kernel. This proves the promised nonuniqueness directly. The canonical globalization theorem requires its exact integral balanced map, not merely a crystal lattice, and remains unchanged.

items.title: Matching the canonical and lower global normalizations in rank one and $A_2$
items.statement:
In rank one the lower global/canonical vectors are exactly F_i^(n), bar fixed and congruent to their normalized crystal classes. Their Kashiwara norms are1/[n]_(q_i²)!, while the transported Lusztig norms are1/∏_(r=1)^n(1−q_i^(2r)); the full color factor is(1−q_i²)^−n. Ordinary F_i^n differs by the nonunit symmetric factorial, and Drinfeld generator normalization includes(q_i−q_i^-1)^−1. This explicitly matches, rather than conflates, the four conventions.
In type A2 degree alpha1+alpha2, the two lower global/canonical vectors are EXACTLY F1F2,F2F1, with no triangular correction. Their Kashiwara Gram matrix is[[1,q],[q,1]], already identity moduloq, and their transported Lusztig Gram is(1−q²)^−2 times this matrix. The Kashiwara upper dual vectors are(1−q²)^−1(F1F2−qF2F1) and(1−q²)^−1(F2F1−qF1F2); they are not the lower vectors. Lusztig form-duals are further multiplied by(1−q²)^2. In degree2alpha1 the lower vector isF1^(2), with the rank-one norm. These computations exhibit the actual convention dictionary and make no false Gram-unimodularity or unspecified correction claim.
items.strategy: Rank one is the unique divided string of1; the corrected balanced theorem gives exactly the divided lower lift, and the already-derived degree-color recursion gives both norms and the Drinfeld scalar. In degree alpha1+alpha2 there is no Serre relation, and e_1′F2=e_2′F1=0. Thus f̃1f̃2·1=F1F2 and f̃2f̃1·1=F2F1, integral/bar fixed with distinct crystal residues. Balanced uniqueness gives them as the exact lifts. Adjunction computes the two diagonals1 and the cross term q (e_1′(F2F1)=qF2), proving the displayed Gram matrix and determinant1−q². Its field inverse gives the two genuine Kashiwara upper duals, not an A-unit inverse. The form dictionary multiplies Gram by(1−q²)^−2 and therefore multiplies dual vectors by its reciprocal. The q0 residues of lower and upper agree, while their A lattices generally differ. The lower degree2alpha1 norm is the exact rank-one1/(1+q²). All displayed finite calculations are complete and consistent with the full canonical comparison supplier.

items.statement: For rank-one V(m omega), use w_n=F^(n)v_m, 0≤n≤m, the lower global basis and lower integral lattice M_A=⊕A w_n. Its normalized polarization has B(w_n,w_s)=delta_ns d_(m,n), with d_(m,n)=q^(n(m−n))[m choose n]_q. Thus its upper form-dual global basis is w_n^up=d_(m,n)^−1w_n and M_A^vee=⊕A d_(m,n)^−1 w_n. These two explicit A-lattices are the object being compared; a numeric finite index is not presumed. For m=1, d=1 at both positions and the bases coincide. For m=2, d_(2,0)=d_(2,2)=1 and d_(2,1)=1+q², so M_A^vee=A w_0⊕A(1+q²)^−1w_1⊕A w_2, properly containing M_A. Its middle quotient is isomorphic to A/(1+q²). Both lattices extend to the same A0 crystal lattice and both basis residues are the same three crystal elements. The upper operators are the weighted adjoints from the duality theorem; their q0 reductions give the same finite string, while exact lower adjunction differs by the displayed norm ratios. The upper basis is fixed by the ADJOINT bar, generally not the ordinary lower bar.

For m=2 the middle norm is q[2]=1+q²; it is not a unit of A, so (1+q²)^−1w_1 is outside the lower lattice. The quotient of its coefficient module by A is isomorphic to A/(1+q²), exhibiting the actual pair of lattices rather than a misleading 'index of E'. At0 this norm is an A0-unit≡1; both basis residues agree. The finite-string ratio formulas then give the exact upper/lower adjoint operators and their modulo-q agreement. Ordinary bar fixes w_1 but sends its upper scalar denominator to(1+q^-2), so only the adjoint bar fixes w_1^up, exactly as the duality theorem states. items.statement:
In V(omega)=L_1(1), let v be highest and w=Fv, with Ev=0,Fv=w,Ew=v,Fw=0,Kv=qv,Kw=q^-1w. Then V_A=Av⊕Aw, L0=A0v⊕A0w, L∞=A∞v⊕A∞w and E_Z=Zv⊕Zw. The integral globalization maps E_Z isomorphically onto the Z-span of its two crystal classes; its rational extension gives the full Q residue. Its lower global basis is v,w. The field string image FV is Q(q)w, its integral image ideal is Aw and its balanced part is Zw.
On V⊗V the exact quasi-R is1+(q−q^-1)E⊗F. Hence Ψ(vv)=vv, Ψ(vw)=vw, Ψ(wv)=wv+(q−q^-1)vw, Ψ(ww)=ww, using concatenation for tensor notation. This preserves total weight and the A tensor lattice and is a semilinear involution. The actual tensor global basis is vv,vw,wv+qvw,ww; raw wv is not bar fixed. Its zero crystal lattice is the A0 tensor lattice and its balanced Z-part is the Z-span of these corrected vectors.
For the mixed free lattice L′=A0(v+w)⊕qA0v with actual infinity chart bar L′=A∞(v+w)⊕q^-1A∞v, the integral balanced part is only Z(v+w); it misses the valid residue class of qv. Thus it is genuinely nonbalanced, although v+w is bar fixed. L′ is not claimed to be a crystal lattice.
items.strategy:
A∩A0=Z[q], A∩A∞=Z[q^-1] and A∩A0∩A∞=Z give the stated balanced parts; q is a unit in A, so A/qA is0 and is never used for the residue. The two chart residues are treated through Z[q]/qZ[q]=Z. Divided powers ofF on this module give only v,w and the higher ones vanish, proving the exact integral lattice. The string-image field/A/Z spaces are distinguished.
The correct generator-normalized field Θ_alpha=(q−q^-1)E⊗F is proved by intertwining, not by c+barc=0 alone. Equivalently applying ΔEΘ=ΘbarΔE to ww gives q vw+wv on the left and q^-1vw+wv+c vw on the right, forcing c=q−q^-1. The map E⊗F sends wv tovw and kills vv,vw,ww, so the four formulas and total-weight preservation follow. Bar twice cancels c+barc=0, verifying involutivity after the scalar is fixed. Directly Ψ(wv+qvw)=wv+(q−q^-1)vw+q^-1vw=wv+qvw. The other three vectors are fixed; their A-transition matrix is unitriangular and their q0 residues are the raw tensor basis, giving the stated global and chart bases.
Put a=v+w,t=v, so V_A=Aa⊕At. In the mixed zero chart the t coefficient has order≥1, while in the ACTUAL bar chart it has infinity order≥1, i.e. Laurent degree≤−1. No nonzero integer Laurent polynomial satisfies both, so E′=Za. Its integral zero residue has independent generators a,qv, and E′ misses exactly the latter. The non-crystal assertions follow from ẽa=v∉L′ and its two weight intersections qA0v,qA0w. No nonexistent class v+qL′ is used.
